question: What else can cause dry eye?
answer:
Other causes of dry eye include: [nei_039_chunk_02].

- Medicines. Dry eye can be a side effect of some medicines that treat conditions like colds and allergies, depression, and high blood pressure [nei_039_chunk_02].

- Health problems [nei_039_chunk_02] ◐. Some health problems — including diabetes, thyroid problems, and autoimmune disorders like lupus or Sjögren syndrome — can cause dry eye [nei_039_chunk_02].

- Laser eye surgery [nei_039_chunk_02] ◐. After some types of laser surgery, your eyes may produce fewer tears [nei_039_chunk_02].

- Windy, smoky, or dry environments [nei_039_chunk_02]. Spending time in these types of places can cause your tears to dry up faster and lead to dry eye [nei_039_chunk_02].

- Looking at screens for long periods of time [nei_039_chunk_02]. You may blink less when looking at computer or tablet screens, which can lead to dry eye [nei_039_chunk_02].

This is general education, not a diagnosis.

See an eye doctor or go to the emergency room now; don't wait for an online answer.

If something is stuck under your eyelid and you can't blink it out, please see your eye doctor or go to the emergency room [nei_025_chunk_03]. Don’t try to remove it yourself — you could scratch your cornea [nei_025_chunk_03].

This is general education, not a diagnosis.

question: What other health problems can blepharitis cause?
answer:
- Stye. A stye is a red, painful bump on the eyelid caused by a blocked oil gland [nei_007_chunk_04].

- Chalazion. A chalazion is a hard, painless lump on the eyelid caused by a blocked oil gland [nei_007_chunk_04].

Oil and flakes can build up in your tear film (a thin layer of tears across the surface of your eye) [nei_007_chunk_04]. This can make your eyes feel dry [nei_007_chunk_04].

- Damage to the cornea [nei_007_chunk_04]. In severe cases, blepharitis can hurt your cornea (the clear outer layer at the front of your eye) [nei_007_chunk_04].

This is general education, not a diagnosis.
removed_claims: Blepharitis can lead to other eye problems, including:
- Dry eye.
- Chronic (long-term) red eye.
Blepharitis can make the white part of your eye look red all the time.

question: I see spots and my vision is sometimes fuzzy. What could it be?
answer:
Please get an eye exam to check for AMD, diabetic retinopathy, or floaters, as these can cause symptoms like spots and blurry vision [nei_015_chunk_01] ◐. Most people have floaters that come and go and often don’t need treatment [nei_015_chunk_01]. Later stages of AMD can cause straight lines to look wavy or crooked and blurry areas in central vision [nei_003_chunk_04] ◐. Early stages of diabetic retinopathy usually don’t have symptoms, but later stages can lead to dark spots or streaks from blood vessels bleeding into the vitreous [nei_004_chunk_02]. Loss of central vision can be a symptom of AMD [nei_003_chunk_04] ◐.

This is general education, not a diagnosis.

question: What causes macular edema?
answer:
Macular edema happens when blood vessels leak into a part of the retina called the macula [nei_005_chunk_02]. The most common cause is diabetic retinopathy — an eye condition that causes vision loss in people with diabetes [nei_005_chunk_02]. If you have diabetic retinopathy, managing your diabetes can help prevent or delay vision loss [nei_005_chunk_02].

This page lists "Other causes of macular edema include", but it doesn’t name them [nei_005_chunk_02]. A page on medicines mentions that "certain medicines, like medicines to treat glaucoma, can cause macular edema as a side effect" [nei_005_chunk_04].

This is general education, not a diagnosis.
caveats: For some people, macular edema only causes mild blurry vision.
If you only have macular edema in 1 eye, it may take longer for you to notice changes to your vision.

question: What is retinal detachment?
answer:
Retinal detachment happens when your retina (a light-sensitive layer of tissue at the back of your eye) is pulled away from its normal position [nei_050_chunk_01]. There are 3 types: rhegmatogenous, tractional, and exudative [nei_050_chunk_01].

This is the most common type of retinal detachment [nei_050_chunk_01]. It can happen if you have a small tear or break in your retina [nei_050_chunk_01].

This happens if scar tissue on your retina pulls your retina away from the back of your eye [nei_050_chunk_02].

This happens when fluid builds up behind your retina, but there aren’t any tears or breaks in your retina [nei_050_chunk_03].

This is general education, not a diagnosis.
caveats: If you have symptoms of a detached retina, go to the eye doctor or the emergency room right away.
If you have diabetes, it’s important to get a comprehensive dilated eye exam at least once a year.

question: What is dry eye?
answer:
Dry eye happens when your eyes don’t make enough tears to stay wet, or when your tears don’t work correctly [nei_006_chunk_01]. This can make your eyes feel uncomfortable, and in some cases it can also cause vision problems [nei_006_chunk_01]. Symptoms can include burning, dry or scratchy feeling, blurry vision, red eyes, and sensitivity to light [nei_006_chunk_01].

question: What are the symptoms of floaters?
answer:
Floaters are small dark shapes that float across your vision [nei_015_chunk_01]. They can look like spots, threads, squiggly lines, or even little cobwebs [nei_015_chunk_01]. Most people have floaters that come and go, and they often don’t need treatment [nei_015_chunk_01].

You may notice floaters more when you look at something bright, like white paper or a blue sky [nei_015_chunk_01].

This is general education, not a diagnosis.

question: What is uveitis?
answer:

This inflammation can cause symptoms like blurry vision, floaters, eye pain, red eyes, and sensitivity to light [nei_021_chunk_02].

question: What happens during LASIK surgery?
answer:
During LASIK surgery, a small flap is cut in the cornea and folded back, allowing the laser to reshape the cornea into the correct shape [nei_049_chunk_03]. The flap is then replaced in place [nei_049_chunk_03] ◐. The procedure is performed after an eye exam that uses a scanner to create a detailed image of the cornea [nei_049_chunk_03].

caveats: Rarely, vision loss from LASIK may be permanent.

question: What’s the treatment for vitreous detachment?

question: How often do I need to get a dilated eye exam?

- Are African American and over age 40 [nei_028_chunk_01].

question: What can I do to prevent diabetic retinopathy?

Having high blood pressure or high cholesterol along with diabetes increases your risk for diabetic retinopathy [nei_004_chunk_07].

question: My newborn's eyes are red and puffy with discharge. Should I wait a few days?
answer:
⚠ Safety notice: sudden vision changes (flashes, many new floaters, a curtain or shadow over your vision, sudden vision loss), an eye injury or something stuck in the eye, severe eye pain, pain or vision getting worse after eye surgery or an injection, or a newborn with eye discharge need care right away. See an eye doctor or go to the emergency room now; don't wait for an online answer.

Call your baby’s doctor now if your baby has unusual fluid (discharge) coming from the eye or puffy red eyelids [nei_047_chunk_01]. Most cases of pink eye get better on their own, but newborns can have serious eye infections from pink eye [nei_008_chunk_05, nei_047_chunk_01]. If symptoms don’t get better after a few days or get worse, see a doctor [nei_008_chunk_05].

This is general education, not a diagnosis.

question: Dilating my pupils for an eye exam is painful, right?
answer:
No. The passages state that dilation is simple and painless [nei_028_chunk_01]. The doctor will give you some eye drops to dilate (widen) your pupil, and it doesn’t hurt [nei_028_chunk_02].

This is general education, not a diagnosis.
caveats: Talk to your doctor about what’s right for you.
It’s the only way to check for eye diseases early on, when they’re easier to treat — and before they cause vision loss.
Even if you think your eyes are healthy, getting a dilated eye exam is the only way to know for sure.

question: How do eye doctors check for RP?
answer:
Eye doctors can check for Retinitis Pigmentosa (RP) as part of a comprehensive dilated eye exam [nei_020_chunk_03]. The exam involves eye drops to dilate the pupil, followed by a visual field test to check peripheral vision [nei_020_chunk_03]. Other tests may include electroretinography (ERG) to check how well the retina responds to light [nei_020_chunk_03].

This is general education, not a diagnosis.
